```{r}
source("R/survival_helpers.R")
source("R/ard_helpers.R")

read_result <- function(file) read.csv(file.path("results", file))
provenance <- yaml::read_yaml(file.path("results", "provenance.yaml"))

attrition  <- read_result("m3_attrition_sql.csv")
first_tx   <- read_result("m4_first_treatment.csv")
tte        <- read_result("m4_tte_summary.csv")
comparison <- read_result("m5_survival_comparison.csv")
dq         <- read_result("m1_dq_checks.csv")
ard_survival <- as.data.frame(arrow::read_parquet(file.path("results", "ard",
                                                             "m6_survival_ard.parquet")))
os <- survival_table_from_ard(ard_survival, survival_analyses[["overall"]])

num <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",")
p3 <- function(x) sprintf("%.3f", x)
os_at <- function(years) {
  row <- os[os$years == years, ]
  paste0(p3(row$survival), " (95% CI ", p3(row$lower_95), " to ", p3(row$upper_95), ")")
}
groups <- aggregate(n_persons ~ FTRTCLS, data = first_tx, FUN = sum)
groups <- groups[match(treatment_levels, groups$FTRTCLS), ]
drug_duplicates <- dq[dq$check_name == "duplicate_records" & dq$table_name == "drug_exposure", ]
```

# OMOP breast cancer walkthrough

Ignacio Garcia Ribelles

This project shows, on synthetic data, the work of a real-world data analyst
in oncology. A breast cancer cohort is extracted with SQL from data in the
OMOP Common Data Model. Conditions and drugs are mapped to standard
vocabularies, and every concept comes from a saved query. Analysis-ready
datasets are built with a data dictionary that records their lineage.
Survival is analysed with correct censoring. The results are stored as
Analysis Results Data (ARD) and the report tables are built from them.
Everything is tested and rebuilt by CI.

All data are synthetic (Synthea). No clinical conclusion may be drawn from
them.

## Headline numbers

Read from `results/` when this file is rendered. Dataset
`` `r provenance$dataset` ``, OMOP CDM `r provenance$cdm_version`,
vocabulary `r provenance$vocabulary_version`.

- **Cohort.** `r num(tail(attrition$n_persons, 1))` people, out of
  `r num(attrition$n_persons[1])` with any breast cancer record. They have a
  first breast cancer record inside observation, at least 365 days of prior
  observation and an age of 18 or over at index. The full attrition table is
  in `results/m3_attrition_sql.csv`.
- **Overall survival.** `r tte$n_events[tte$PARAMCD == "OS"]` deaths. Survival
  is `r os_at(1)` at 1 year and `r os_at(5)` at 5 years.
- **First treatment within 90 days.**
  `r paste(paste0(groups$FTRTCLS, " ", groups$n_persons), collapse = ", ")`.
- **Two routes to one estimate.** CohortSurvival and a hand-built
  `survival::survfit` agree to 3 decimal places. The largest difference is
  `r format(max(abs(comparison$difference)), digits = 1)`.
- **Data quality.** `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * drug_duplicates$share_failing)`
  of drug records repeat another record with the same person, drug, start date
  and type. They are reported, not removed.

## How to run it

You need R 4.4 or later and the [Quarto](https://quarto.org) command-line tool.

1. Clone the repository and open R in its folder.
2. Restore the packages with `renv::restore()`.
3. Copy `.Renviron.example` to `.Renviron` and set `EUNOMIA_DATA_FOLDER` to
   an absolute path. The data are downloaded there and never committed.
4. Build everything and run the tests with `Rscript run_all.R`. The first run
   downloads about 800 MB.
5. Render the report with `quarto render report/report.qmd`.

`Rscript tools/lint.R` lints the code. `Rscript
tools/check_results_unchanged.R` checks that a rebuild gives the committed
results. CI runs all of this on every push.

## How it fits together

``` mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph cdm["OMOP CDM in DuckDB"]
    clinical["person, observation_period,<br/>condition_occurrence,<br/>drug_exposure, death"]
    vocab["concept, concept_ancestor,<br/>concept_relationship"]
  end
  clinical --> dq["Data-quality checks<br/>sql/dq"]
  vocab --> codelists["Concept sets<br/>codelists"]
  clinical --> cohort["Cohort<br/>SQL and CohortConstructor"]
  codelists --> cohort
  cohort --> adam["adsl_like and adtte_like<br/>data-dictionary.yaml"]
  adam --> analyses["Table 1, Kaplan-Meier,<br/>landmark analysis"]
  analyses --> ard["Analysis Results Data<br/>results/ard"]
  ard --> report["Report tables<br/>report/report.qmd"]
```

| Step | Milestone | Code |
|----|----|----|
| Row counts and data-quality checks | M1 | `sql/explore`, `sql/dq`, `R/10_explore_dq.R` |
| Concept sets and mapping | M2 | `sql/codelists`, `R/20_codelists.R` |
| Cohort, built twice | M3 | `sql/cohort`, `R/30_cohort.R` |
| `adsl_like` and `adtte_like` | M4 | `sql/analysis`, `R/40_analysis_data.R`, `data-dictionary.yaml` |
| Table 1, Kaplan-Meier, immortal-time bias | M5 | `R/50_analyses.R`, `R/survival_helpers.R` |
| Analysis Results Data | M6 | `R/60_ard.R`, `R/ard_helpers.R` |
| Provenance, lint and CI | M7 | `R/provenance.R`, `tools`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml` |

Every results file carries the git commit and vocabulary version that produced
it. The commit is the one checked out during the run, so committed results
point to the commit before them.

## Limitations

- The data are synthetic. They come from one Synthea dataset and support no
  clinical conclusion.
- The cohort is small, and some treatment groups hold fewer than 10 people.
  Estimates are imprecise.
- Many observation periods start on the day of the breast cancer record. Those
  people fail the 365-day rule, which removes most of the people with a record.
- Chronic conditions appear to be recorded once, around onset. Comorbidity
  flags therefore use all history before index, not a 365-day look-back.
- The data contain no ICD-10 or ICD-10-CM codes. The ICD-10-CM mapping is shown
  from the vocabulary alone.
- Time to first treatment is censored at death. Death is really a competing
  risk, so this is a simplification.
- The datasets follow ADaM naming as a convention only. They are not
  CDISC-conformant, and nothing here is validated.
